correctness.rationale: For any connected positively weighted bipartite graph, the conjugate signless Laplacian is irreducible and nonnegative. Perron–Frobenius makes \(\lambda\) simple, while connectedness gives \(Q>0\). The exact Hessian integral is strictly below the spectral upper bound at \(h=2/\lambda\) along every moving step, excluding all nontrivial periodic orbits through the endpoint; compactness forces omega-limit points to equilibria. Oddness and analytic implicit-function reduction at antiphase yield \(x_\mu=\sqrt{3\lambda\mu/Q}\,v+O(\mu^{3/2})\), with an invertible transverse linearization because the remaining Laplacian eigenvalues lie in \((0,\lambda)\). The Jacobians at the two points coincide. Their critical multiplier is \(-1+2\mu+O(\mu^2)\), while all other quotient multipliers are strictly inside the unit circle. The embedded `verify.py` was replayed on seven bipartite graphs with 3,689 numerical checks; numerical evidence does not prove an all-graph assertion.

originality.rationale: The motivating source proves potential decrease only for \(0<h<2/\lambda\) and Corollary 5.3 establishes loss of antiphase stability for \(h>2/\lambda\) on trees, without constructing an attracting replacement. Litman's general gradient-descent theory already establishes abstract local square-root period-two branching, so that mechanism alone is covered prior work. The reviewed full claim additionally verifies critical simplicity and the quartic sign across all connected positive-weight bipartite topologies, establishes transverse attraction with a leading Floquet coefficient, and includes strict global no-periodicity at \(h=2/\lambda\). Comparison of the actual primary statements does not show the complete stronger result to be implied; potential unindexed equivalences remain a residual risk.

value.rationale: The motivating network paper identifies the sharp descent bound \(h_c=2/\lambda\) and loss of the antiphase sink above it, without identifying the subsequent attractor. The present theorem proves a topology- and weight-uniform sharp transition: no nonfixed periodic orbit occurs through the critical endpoint, while an attracting primitive period-two orbit is born for every connected positively weighted bipartite network immediately above it. The graph quartic gives a quantitative square-root amplitude and the two-step critical Floquet multiplier \(1-4\mu+O(\mu^2)\). This links a global Lyapunov barrier to a nontrivial recurrent birth, beyond a fixed-point multiplier or arbitrary finite example; distant postcritical dynamics and Morse–Smale transversality remain open.
